covers: Changes since the 09:25 update: gold, silver, dollar and the rand to about 10:00 SAST Wednesday 4 November (JSE closed today for local elections)
headline: Gold breaks through $4,000 an ounce as Democrats take both houses of Congress; US futures hold most of their overnight recovery
summary: The JSE is closed for local elections, but the rand is firmer offshore at about R16.56/$, up 0.3% on the day, as the dollar weakens (Trading Economics, 4 Nov). In the US, AP's count gives Democrats 53 Senate seats and CNN and CBS project a Democratic House; Nasdaq-100 futures were down 0.6% at 08:24 SAST after falling more than 2% earlier, with AMD up on results (Investing.com; The National, 4 Nov). Spot gold rose 1.78% to $4,000.21 and December silver futures 4.2% to $51.67 at about 08:36 SAST, a supportive set-up for JSE gold and PGM miners when trading resumes on Thursday (FinanceFeeds, 4 Nov).

items.title: Democrats take both houses of Congress: AP count gives them 53 Senate seats; CNN and CBS project the House
items.summary: AP called the Senate for Democrats late on Tuesday US time after Josh Turek won Iowa (Forbes, 4 Nov). By AP's running count at about 08:24 SAST Democrats had 53 Senate seats to the Republicans' 42, with 5 uncalled (Investing.com, 4 Nov). The House was projected for Democrats by CNN and CBS, and earlier by Decision Desk HQ; they needed to flip only three Republican seats and easily exceeded that (The National, 4 Nov). Reuters' Morning Bid also notes the Texas governorship flipped to Democrats, which analysts see as a risk to data-centre expansion in the state. A Democratic Congress makes new tax-cut or spending laws from the White House harder to pass.
items.source: Forbes, 4 Nov 2026; Investing.com, 4 Nov 2026; The National, 4 Nov 2026; Reuters Morning Bid via Investing.com, 4 Nov 2026

items.title: Futures pare losses: Nasdaq-100 −0.6%, S&P 500 −0.39%, Dow −0.18% at 08:24 SAST
items.summary: At 01:24 New York time (08:24 SAST) S&P 500 futures were down 0.39% at 7,565.50, Nasdaq-100 futures down 0.6% at 28,135.0 and Dow futures down 0.18% at 51,801.0, after falling between 1% and 2.5% earlier in the night (Investing.com, 4 Nov). The Morning brief had Nasdaq-100 futures down 2.26% at 06:24 SAST. In Asia the damage was larger: Japan's Nikkei fell 3.5% and South Korea's Kospi 3.6% (The National, 04:33 UTC).

items.title: Treasury yields fall: 10-year down 7 basis points to 4.89%
items.summary: Investors bought US government bonds for safety as the results came in; the 10-year Treasury yield fell 7 basis points to 4.89% (The National, 4 Nov). Lower US yields usually help emerging-market bonds, including South Africa's.

items.title: Today: US ISM data, September trade balance and the Treasury refunding plan; McDonald's, Uber, Qualcomm and Arm report
items.summary: Reuters' Morning Bid lists the US ISM survey for October, the September trade balance, euro-area inflation, a Riksbank rate decision and the US Treasury's quarterly refunding announcement for Wednesday. Investing.com lists McDonald's, Arm Holdings, Qualcomm and Uber among today's results, and notes CVS is in focus after reports it plans to split in two by 2028.
items.source: Reuters Morning Bid via Investing.com, 4 Nov 2026; Investing.com, 4 Nov 2026

items.title: Tuesday close: Nasdaq +0.83% to 25,372.01, S&P 500 +0.36% to 7,568.92, Dow −0.38% to 51,786.72
items.summary: Tech led on Tuesday 3 November before the election results: the Nasdaq Composite closed up 0.83% at 25,372.01 and the S&P 500 up 0.36% at 7,568.92, while the Dow fell 0.38% to 51,786.72. The gains were wiped out in overnight futures trade as the midterm results came in.

items.title: JSE closed today for local elections; rand firmer offshore at about R16.56/$
items.summary: South Africans vote in municipal elections today, Wednesday 4 November, and the JSE is closed. Offshore the rand traded at R16.5579/$ on Wednesday, 0.29% firmer on the day, helped by a weaker dollar and firmer precious metals (Trading Economics, 4 Nov). On Tuesday at 15:04 SAST the rand was at R16.6425/$, the Top 40 was down about 0.7% and the 2035 bond yield fell 1.5 basis points to 8.52% (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 3 Nov). JSE shares react to the US results on Thursday.
items.source: Trading Economics, 4 Nov 2026; CNBC Africa (Reuters), 3 Nov 2026

items.title: New fuel prices in force from today: diesel down R1.10–R1.20 a litre, petrol down 1c
items.summary: From 00:01 on Wednesday 4 November, 93 and 95 petrol fall 1c a litre, diesel 0.05% falls R1.10 and diesel 0.005% R1.20, while illuminating paraffin (wholesale) rises R2.75 a litre and LPGas R1.83/kg, per the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources. The general fuel levy cut (R1.50/l petrol, R3/l diesel) is partly offset by a new slate levy of 135.84c/l. Cheaper diesel helps transport, farming and mining costs (Stuff, 3 Nov).

items.title: US letter gives 60 days' notice: SA's AGOA status to end on 1 January 2027
items.summary: BusinessTech reports that President Trump wrote to President Ramaphosa giving 60 days' notice that South Africa's AGOA trade beneficiary status will end on 1 January 2027, citing slow progress on corruption and trade barriers, and foreign policy concerns. Exporters of vehicles, citrus and other farm goods are the most exposed. On Monday the rand gained about 0.4% to R16.64/$ and traded at R16.62/$ on Tuesday morning; the Top-40 rose about 1% and the 2035 bond yield fell 2.5 basis points to 8.565%. NAAMSA new vehicle sales rose 10.4% year on year in October.

items.title: Dollar index −0.6% to a one-month low of 101.27; euro $1.1258, yen 157.92
items.summary: Reuters reported the dollar index down 0.6% at 101.27, a one-month low, on worries a Democratic Congress will add AI regulation; the euro rose 0.6% to $1.1258, sterling 0.3% to $1.3458 and the yen strengthened nearly 0.8% to 157.92 per dollar (Reuters via Investing.com, 4 Nov). A weaker dollar usually supports the rand, which trades offshore today with the JSE closed.

items.title: Gold through $4,000: spot +1.78% to $4,000.21; silver futures +4.2% to $51.67
items.summary: At 06:36 GMT (08:36 SAST) December COMEX gold futures traded at $4,027.30, up 2.2%, and spot gold crossed $4,000 at $4,000.21, up 1.78% on the day; December silver futures rose about 4.2% to $51.67, and the US dollar index was at 101.50, down from 101.87 (FinanceFeeds, 4 Nov). The move follows the Democratic sweep of Congress and lower Treasury yields. At 08:11 SAST platinum was up 1% at $1,432.93 and palladium up 1.7% at $952.50 (Investing.com, 4 Nov). A firmer gold and PGM basket is a better set-up for JSE gold and PGM miners when trading resumes on Thursday.

items.title: Oil steadies: Brent $103.60, WTI $95.98 as Gulf supply worries return
items.summary: Oilprice.com had Brent at $103.60 and WTI at $95.98 on Wednesday morning after Tuesday's sharp fall on signs Iran might discuss issues it had ruled out. Vortexa data show October exports through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 17.1 million barrels a day, down from 18.9 million in September, and Rystad Energy said Gulf flows are unlikely to return to normal soon even with a US–Iran deal. Lower oil helps SA fuel prices; higher oil works the other way.

items.title: AMD (LRC Stock Scanner: HOLD, target $641.00) ends after-hours at $508.20, up 5%, after its beat
items.summary: AMD closed regular trade on 3 November at $483.90, reached $530.38 after hours and finished after-hours trading at $508.20, up 5.0% (FinanceFeeds, 06:55 GMT 4 Nov). Third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $13.38 billion, data centre revenue nearly doubled to $8.55 billion and fourth-quarter guidance of about $17 billion beat consensus of $16.23 billion (AMD; Investing.com, 3 Nov). The after-hours price is still well below the scanner's $641.00 target; the HOLD rating is not changed here.
items.source: FinanceFeeds, 4 Nov 2026; AMD, 3 Nov 2026; Investing.com, 3 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: Super Micro (LRC Stock Scanner: HOLD, target $62.57) up more than 4% overnight on results
items.summary: Super Micro shares were up more than 4% in overnight trade after first-quarter revenue nearly quadrupled to about $20 billion, per Stocktwits (3 Nov). On 20 October the company had pre-announced revenue of $18.5–19.5 billion and a 12.0–12.5% gross margin, above its earlier guide of $14.5–15.5 billion (Supermicro, 20 Oct). The scanner shows HOLD with a $62.57 target against a last price of $31.29 (3 Nov). The rating is not changed here.
items.source: Stocktwits via Yahoo Finance, 3 Nov 2026; Supermicro, 20 Oct 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: NVIDIA (BUY, target $239.30) and Meta (HOLD, target $547.40): Nasdaq-100 futures loss narrows to 0.6%
items.summary: Overnight selling hit AI build-out stocks on fears a Democratic Congress, and a Democratic Texas governor, will slow data-centre construction (Reuters Morning Bid, 4 Nov). Nasdaq-100 futures have since narrowed their loss to 0.6% at 08:24 SAST (Investing.com, 4 Nov). The scanner shows NVIDIA at BUY with a $239.30 target (last $207.80) and Meta at HOLD with a $547.40 target (last $620.20), from the 3 Nov 18:45 SAST run. Individual pre-market prices were not verified, so none are given. Ratings are not changed here.
items.source: Reuters Morning Bid via Investing.com, 4 Nov 2026; Investing.com, 4 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 3 Nov 2026
